QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_27

question.text: Which statement correctly describes the base on which management fees are typically charged in an Indian Cat III AIF?

answer.text: Committed capital, regardless of whether called
Gross Net Asset Value (GNAV) at the end of the period, typically 1% to 2.5%
Only the profit above the hurdle rate
Residual value of unrealised investments (RVPI) only

explanation.text: The Logic: Cat III AIFs charge management fees as a percentage (1.0–2.5%) of GNAV (Gross Net Asset Value) at period-end. This is different from Cat I/II PE funds, which often charge fees on committed capital. The Trap: A is the Cat I/II PE model — not Cat III. C confuses fee with incentive. D mixes up fee base with a PE multiple. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D (Cat I/II Manager) tests committed-capital fee base; XIX-E tests Cat III's GNAV base. Recognising the distinction is a core XIX-E exam skill. Manager's Pro-Tip: Negotiate a tiered management-fee schedule (e.g., 1.75% below INR 500 cr, 1.50% above) so the fund remains scalable. LPs love discount tiers for anchor commitments.
